turbine to optimize chemistry control and reduce corrosion and deposition.

from the contaminates, increasing the number of chemical excursions and
high down time in repairing the affected plant due to corrosion and
deposition. Modification for time was also approved from 8 September 2024

longer in an acceptable condition and the lift cannot be returned back to
operation with the current state of these ropes. After the Station flooding
incident in 2021, the ropes were replaced and both lifts put back in
operation. Drakensberg experiences seepage water in the lift shaft from
time to time especially during rainy seasons. This risk was mitigated by
putting the gutters around the lift shaft which channel the seepage water
down to the drainage sump. Drakensberg had a severe water leak from the
potable water pipe that runs along the lift shaft which caused the main ropes
on Lift B to be badly rusted. The potable water pipe has been fixed and Lift
B has been out of service for approximately a year due to damaged ropes.
Main ropes are classified as safety components of the lifts, it is therefore
highly recommended that the rusted ropes be replaced. Lift A that is in
operation has been over utilized since Lift B has been out of service.
Drakensberg is currently having back-to-back outages and for longer
durations which then also puts more strain on Lift A.
